Logger implements PSR-3. Stream output runs on the calling fiber and propagates formatting and write errors.
The default minimum level is `info`. Pass `minLevel` to change it.

## Installation

```shell
composer require thesis/logger
```

Requires 64-bit PHP 8.6+.

## Usage

```php
use Thesis\Logger;
use function Thesis\Io\stderr;

$logger = new Logger(stderr());
$logger->info('Worker {worker} is ready', ['worker' => 3]);
```

## Output formats

`Formatter\Json` is the default. Each NDJSON line has `time` (RFC 3339 with microseconds), `level`, `message`
and a `context` object. Scalar fields keep their JSON types.

Use `Formatter\Console` for a text line with a timestamp, a colored level label, the message and any context.
By default, the console omits fields already used in the message. When every field was used, the line ends with the
message. Pass `removeUsedContextFields: false` to print the full context. Pass `colors: false` for plain text.

```php
use Thesis\Logger\Formatter\Console;
use Thesis\Logger\StreamHandler;

$logger = new Logger(new StreamHandler(stderr(), new Console()));
```

Implement `Formatter::format(Record $record)` to provide your own format. The stream handler calls it with the
`DateTimeImmutable` captured at the log call, the interpolated message and the normalized context.
Return the formatted record. `StreamHandler` appends `\n` and writes the result to the stream.

During capture, formatting and output, a stream handler ignores calls back into the same handler,
including calls from tasks started in that context. Independent tasks can still log through it.

## Time and timezone

`Logger` snapshots the time from its PSR-20 `ClockInterface` in the calling fiber before converting the message. The default `Thesis\Time\WallClock` uses the
PHP default timezone. Both built-in formatters preserve the offset returned by the clock. Pass your own clock
to control the timestamp, or use `WallClock` with a fixed timezone.

```php
use Thesis\Time\WallClock;

$logger = new Logger(stderr(), clock: new WallClock(new DateTimeZone('UTC')));
```

## Messages and context

Scalar context values fill matching `{key}` placeholders in every format. Missing keys stay in the message.
The context keeps its fields after interpolation. An exception under
`exception` becomes an object with `type`, `message`, `file` and `line`. Other objects, arrays and resources in the context
are represented by their type. A `Stringable` message is cast to a string on the calling fiber.
Non-finite floats are written as `null`. The logger considers the first 32 entries, skips keys with invalid
UTF-8, a leading NUL or more than 128 bytes, and limits text to 1024 bytes. If an exception carries a
non-scalar message, the exception summary uses its type. Unset file and line fields become `''` and `0`.
